overview.text: The Many-banded Krait is an extremely venomous snake of southern China, Taiwan and South-east Asia. It is shy and calm, but a bite is a medical emergency.

identification.text: Black or bluish-black with many white bands; smooth, glossy scales and a ridge along the back.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 1 to 1.5 m long, up to 1.85 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Taiwan, southern China (including Hong Kong and Hainan), Myanmar, Laos, northern Vietnam and probably Thailand.

behaviour.text: Active at night and more defensive then; by day it hides under stones or in holes. It hibernates from November to April.

reproduction.text: Mates in August-September; females lay 3 to 15 eggs.

recognise.text: Black with many narrow white bands.
